note: Route lines are drawn by hand for this map and distances are computed from the drawn line. Treat every figure as an approximate value for planning, not a measured course.

loops.name: Tiergarten classic
loops.surface: crushed gravel and firm park paths
loops.character: The big green loop every Berlin runner ends up on. Wide paths, old trees, and the Victory Column halfway round.
loops.water: Kiosks at the Neuer See cafe side in the daytime; carry your own bottle early.
loops.afterDarkNote: Side paths are unlit once you leave the main axis. After dark, stay on Strasse des 17. Juni itself.

bands.short: Cut across at the Grosser Stern for a shorter out-and-back on the main axis.
bands.middle: One full round as drawn is the natural distance here.
bands.long: Add the Spreeweg arm past Bellevue Palace or run a second inner round.

loops.name: Museum Island sunrise round
loops.character: The old East Berlin centre with the Dom, Museum Island and the Nikolaiviertel to yourself. Before 08:00 this is the emptiest famous square kilometre in Berlin.
loops.water: Bakeries and kiosks open from about 07:00 around Hackescher Markt.
loops.afterDarkNote: City streets stay lit all night; watch the cobbles when they are wet.

bands.short: One round as drawn is already the point. Walk the last stretch and look up.
bands.middle: Run it twice, once on each bank of the Spree.
bands.long: Extend along the Spree promenade toward the East Side Gallery and back.

loops.name: Tempelhofer Feld ring
loops.station: U Suedstern or U Boddinstrasse, then a short walk
loops.character: An entire former airfield with no cars, no corners and a horizon. The closest thing Berlin has to a running track the size of a district.
loops.water: No taps on the field itself; bring a bottle, especially in wind and sun.
loops.afterDarkNote: The gates close at 20:30 in September and open again at 06:00.

bands.short: Run one runway straight and come back along the other.
bands.long: Two rings, or one ring plus both runway straights.

loops.name: Landwehrkanal towpath
loops.station: U Prinzenstrasse or U Kottbusser Tor
loops.surface: packed gravel and pavement under plane trees
loops.character: Kreuzberg's shaded water line past Admiralbruecke and the Maybachufer. Cafes, canoes and swans the whole way.
loops.water: Cafes and Spaetis line the banks; the Tuesday and Friday market at Maybachufer makes that stretch a walk, not a run.
loops.afterDarkNote: Stretches between bridges are dim after dark; the pavement side of the Ufer streets is the better line at night.

bands.middle: Turn around at the Ohlauer Strasse bridge.
bands.long: Run the full drawn line to Lohmuehlenbruecke and back.

loops.name: Treptower Park and the Spree
loops.surface: broad paved promenade and park paths
loops.character: River air, the bridge to the Insel der Jugend, and the vast Soviet War Memorial on the way back. The most cinematic easy run in the city.
loops.water: Kiosks by the harbour and at the island bridge in season.
loops.afterDarkNote: The riverside is quiet and dark late in the evening; go at golden hour instead.

bands.short: Turn at the Insel der Jugend bridge and come straight back along Puschkinallee.
bands.middle: One full round as drawn, through the memorial axis.
bands.long: Continue along the Spree into Plaenterwald forest before looping back.

loops.name: Volkspark Friedrichshain round
loops.station: Tram M5, M6 or M8 at Platz der Vereinten Nationen
loops.surface: smooth park paths, one real hill
loops.character: East Berlin's oldest park with the 78-metre rubble hill in the middle. The short loop with an honest climb when you want effort, not distance.
loops.water: Cafe Schoenbrunn sits right on the loop in the daytime.
loops.afterDarkNote: The main round is busier and better lit than most Berlin parks in the evening, but the hill paths go dark first.

bands.middle: Two rounds, or one round plus the climb over the Grosser Bunkerberg.
bands.long: Lap it and add the hill each time; three rounds with the climb is a serious session.
